newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares snap three-day losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares snap three-day losing streak.

text.p: Slovenian shares rebounded on Tuesday after three days of losses, with the index boosted by gains in market heavyweights BTC and Kolinska.
But traders said continued uncertainty on the market would likely keep price moves confined to narrow ranges.

The SBI index firmed 0.37 percent or 4.81 points to 1,302.60. Overall eight shares rose, four fell and three were flat, while 13 were untraded. Turnover jumped to 52.1 million tolars from 27.1 million.

"Today's volume was again very low because most traders went to the bourse's annual seminar. As there are still some unsolved questions hurting the market, a standstill could last at least for another week," said Tone Glavan, a trader at brokerage Bema.

He said uncertainty surrounding the ratification of Slovenia's association agreement with the EU and the implementation of custodian accounts will continuing stemming the flow of fresh foreign capital from the bourse over the short-term.
In February the central bank blocked foreign buying, demanding international investors to open special share trading custody accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 licensed banks.
Since then the blue-chip index has lost over 21 percent, while the average daily volume has shrunk to a third of its previous size.
Traders said failure to ratify association agreement with the EU could also keep foreign investors away over the summer, pushing the index down to its December levels of about 1,150 points.
Parliament last week postponed a vote on whether to ratify an EU association accord, signed in June 1996, in order to allow more time to reach a broader agreement on the issue.
Food maker Kolinska was the most active share, firming 0.37 percent to 1,907 tolars on volume of 7,040 shares for total turnover of 13.5 million.
Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the top gainer, rising 3.54 percent to 13,150 tolars on volume of 60 shares.
Traders said Salus rose in expectation of a dividend payout.
Aroma producer Etol led the day's decliners, falling 2.13 percent to 17,000 tolars on volume of seven shares.
"Fall on such a low volume is not significant enough, most probably an individual shareholder was selling," one broker said.
Warehouse and shopping centre operator BTC closed 1.40 percent or 200 tolars higher at 14,490 tolars on volume of 790 shares for total turnover of 11.3 million tolars.
Market participants said BTC was up on expectations that it would issue global depository receipts (GDR) early next month.
BTC has declined any comment on a possible GDR issue.
